evidence.note: ZoomR fine-tunes a reasoning model to summarize its own thoughts after each paragraph, then at inference dynamically retrieves only a small, consensus-selected subset of full-resolution reasoning segments (zooming in) while keeping the rest as compressed summary keys -- cutting KV-cache GPU memory more than 4x versus a full cache with accuracy close to the vanilla full-KV baseline, and finds that attention-head consensus on which segments matter is itself a diagnostic signal correlated with answer correctness.
evidence.title: ZoomR: Memory Efficient Reasoning through Multi-Granularity Key Value Retrieval
